Title: AutoDAN: Interpretable Gradient-Based Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models

This paper introduces AutoDAN, an interpretable adversarial attack on large language models (LLMs) that merges the strengths of manual jailbreak attacks and adversarial attacks. AutoDAN uses gradient-based optimization to generate interpretable and universal adversarial suffixes from scratch, which can jailbreak common LLMs while maintaining high attack success rates and low perplexity. The proposed attack can bypass perplexity filters and transfer to black-box LLMs better than unreadable counterparts. The work offers a new way to red-team LLMs and understand jailbreak mechanisms via interpretability.

Summary of Attack Methods:

The paper "AutoDAN: Interpretable Gradient-Based Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models" presents a new approach to jailbreak attacks on large language models (LLMs) that combines the strengths of both manual jailbreak attacks and adversarial attacks. The proposed method, called AutoDAN, uses gradient-based optimization to generate interpretable and universal adversarial suffixes from scratch, which can bypass perplexity filters and achieve high attack success rates. The key features of AutoDAN include left-to-right token-by-token prompt generation, a two-step optimization process, and a simple method to combine jailbreaking and readability objectives. The paper demonstrates the versatility of AutoDAN by automatically leaking system prompts using a customized objective and shows that the interpretable attack prompts generated by AutoDAN transfer better to black-box models than unreadable ones. The main contributions of the paper are the introduction of AutoDAN, an interpretable gradient-based adversarial attack on LLMs, and the demonstration of its effectiveness in jailbreaking common LLMs while maintaining lower perplexity than previous attacks.

Introduction to the Mechanism of Success

The paper "AutoDAN: Interpretable Gradient-Based Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models" introduces a new approach to jailbreak attacks on large language models (LLMs) that combines the strengths of both manual jailbreak attacks and adversarial attacks. The proposed method, called AutoDAN, uses gradient-based optimization to generate interpretable and universal adversarial suffixes from scratch, which can bypass perplexity filters and achieve high attack success rates. The key features of AutoDAN include left-to-right token-by-token prompt generation, a two-step optimization process, and a simple method to combine jailbreaking and readability objectives. The paper also discusses the limitations of current solutions to jailbreak attacks and the potential risks of LLMs being misused.

The main contributions of the paper are:

1. The introduction of AutoDAN, an interpretable gradient-based adversarial attack on LLMs that merges the strengths of manual jailbreak attacks and adversarial attacks.
2. The proposal of a two-step optimization process to optimize each individual token, considering both jailbreaking and readability objectives.
3. The development of a simple method to combine the jailbreaking and readability objectives, achieving adaptability to token distribution's entropy.

Overall, the paper offers a new way to red-team LLMs and understand jailbreak mechanisms via interpretability, and demonstrates the versatility of AutoDAN by automatically leaking system prompts using a customized objective.

Related Work:

Several recent studies have proposed solutions to address the vulnerabilities of large language models (LLMs) to jailbreak attacks. These solutions include:

1. Effective manual jailbreak attacks are limited and often posted online, and API providers can blacklist known attack prompts to patch existing vulnerabilities (Perez & Ribeiro, 2022; Greshake et al., 2023).
2. Adversarial attacks generate unlimited but unreadable gibberish prompts, detectable by perplexity-based filters (Zou et al., 2023b).
3. Current adversarial attacks produce prompt texts that appear gibberish to humans, and using perplexity filters can effectively detect them (Alon & Kamfonas, 2023).

However, these solutions may be too optimistic, as they do not take into account the possibility of an automatic adversarial attack that is interpretable and bypasses perplexity filters. In this paper, the authors propose an interpretable adversarial attack on LLMs, named AutoDAN, which addresses the challenges of jailbreaking and readability objectives. AutoDAN uses a two-step, preliminary-to-fine process to optimize each individual token, with each step considering both jailbreaking and readability objectives. The authors show that AutoDAN can generate readable prompts that bypass perplexity filters and achieve high attack success rates.

Overall, the related work in this area has focused on developing solutions to address the vulnerabilities of LLMs to jailbreak attacks, but these solutions may not be effective against interpretable adversarial attacks like AutoDAN. The authors propose a new way to red-team LLMs and understand jailbreak mechanisms via interpretability, which offers a promising direction for future research.
